verdicts.reason: X measures the writer's own prior contact history with the agency while Y measures coordination with other commenters, and a first-time joint coalition filing would score high on Y and zero on X.
Both count the same evidence -- prior meetings, earlier submissions, ongoing exchanges with agency staff -- as the sign of a continuing rather than one-off relationship with the agency.
Both score the presence of costly document-production artifacts (exhibits, indexes/inventories, slide decks, formal packaging) and would move together on essentially the same cues.

X credits any broader docket-lifecycle engagement including extensions, supplemental filings, and replies to other commenters, so a comment engaging the docket without any agency-personnel relationship scores high on X and low on Y.
Citing CFR parts and sections is a formal-precision cue that is independent of whether any statutory-authority argument is developed.
Both ask whether the comment sets out a concrete alternative regulatory design specific enough to be implemented, versus merely objecting.

Y rewards any organizational-scale figures including a single firm's revenue, staffing, and facilities, whereas X requires a represented constituency or signatory base, so a lone large corporation scores high on Y and low on X.

X keys on evidence of joint action (named coalition, joint campaign, multiple signatories) while Y keys on magnitude claims, so a two-organization joint letter with no membership numbers scores high on X and low on Y.
The two instructions enumerate nearly identical cues -- prior meetings, collaboration, earlier submissions, direct agency exchanges -- and differ only in wording.
Emotional intensity and first-hand operational experience are independent: a dispassionate operator's account scores high on Y and low on X, and an outraged bystander the reverse.
Both score the same display of stacked degrees, titles, certifications, and appointments by the author or signatories.
Both require self-derived numeric compliance-cost figures with the basis or source stated, and score zero when no numbers appear.
Both measure whether the comment presents itself as a continuing turn in an existing agency relationship via prior filings, meetings, and ongoing contacts.
